q: Why is a Coimbatore induction foundry's CBAM figure much lower than its carbon footprint?
title: Induction foundry: CBAM vs footprint
short: Because CBAM counts only direct emissions for iron and steel goods, and an induction furnace's energy is electricity, which is left out. The CBAM figure is mostly the pig iron or other covered precursors charged; the full footprint adds the electricity, often about as much again.
audience: Induction foundries making pump, valve and motor castings in the Coimbatore cluster

ul: CBAM figure: direct emissions plus covered precursors, for an EU importer's declaration.
Product footprint: also counts electricity and other inputs, for buyers reporting Scope 3.

p: Send the CBAM figure only where the casting is declared under a CBAM code such as 7325. For pump and valve bodies declared under chapter 84, the buyer needs no CBAM data today but may still ask for the footprint.
Melting efficiency in kWh per tonne, yield, and the scrap share in the charge drive both figures. Renewable power bought through open access lowers the market-based footprint but not the CBAM figure.

example.title: Worked example: one tonne of good castings (illustrative inputs)
lines: Pig iron charged: 0.20 t x 2.00 t CO2e per t = 0.40 t CO2e (CBAM figure)
Electricity: 700 kWh x 0.710 (FY 2024-25 grid factor) = 0.497 t CO2 (footprint only)
example.note: Quantities and the pig iron figure are illustrative.
